name: Mbato
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Bogny, Yapo Joseph 1994. La syntaxe du ngwla (mbato). These 3eme cycle, Universite d'Abidjan, 321pp (per Glottolog MED long_grammar); not online.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en). 'Mbato language', revision of 6 Aug 2025 (phonology section sourced to Bôle-Richard 2018 and Bôle-Richard 1984)
sources.note: Tertiary. 'Mbato has a tonal system consisting of three level tones' (citing Bôle-Richard 2018); no nasal consonant phonemes; nothing at all on stress or accent.
Bibliographic only: confirms Thomas Blecke's talk 'Verb inflection in Nghlwa (/Mbato)'; no abstracts or papers are posted on the conference site.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid page and BibTeX records for mbat1247 (refs 133148 Bogny 1994; 314181 Konan & Mando 2006; 126286 Grassias & Bolé-Richard 1983; 110124 Bolé-Richard 1984; 672346 Blecke 2018; 585711 Ahiman 2001; 658505 Bôle-Richard 2018; 18498 Stewart 1989)
sources.note: Bibliographic only: six descriptive references, none with a URL/DOI; the only phonology item is Konan & Mando 2006 (Köppe chapter, pp. 311-325); the sketch is Grassias & Bolé-Richard 1983 in the Atlas des langues kwa (pp. 465-506); the 'grammar' is Bogny 1994, a 321-pp syntax thesis.

sources.citation: Delafosse, Maurice. 1904. Vocabulaires comparatifs de plus de 60 langues ou dialectes parlés à la Côte d'Ivoire et dans les régions limitrophes. Paris: Leroux. (includes a Gwa = M'Batto vocabulary collected 1903 at Bingerville)
sources.note: Only a general remark covering all 66 languages, p. 3: « Quant à l'accent tonique ou plutôt l'intonation, dont l'importance est souvent considérable dans les langues nègres... il est impossible de donner ces indications au moyen de signes alphabétiques. » Nothing Mbato-specific; p. 11 ethnographic note says the Gwa language is very close to Kyama (Ebrié).
